answer: A strong anti-sybil design is stake-backed identity with peer attestation: every agent must lock a deposit in escrow before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities. Like a bridge that only lets one convoy cross at a time, the escrow throttles cheap copies, because each new identity costs real capital. Honest agents build a reputation trail over time, so the economy stays a clear lagoon where legitimate work flows in through a single narrow inlet that is easy to watch, while cheap fakes drown in their own costs before extracting value.
